origin: Built by Muse (AI assistant) on 18 November 2026 at Steven Powell's request for a physics room, 'Everyday Physics' — the last of the science trio he named (after Everyday Chemistry and Everyday Electronics): a playable pool table with the physics drawn on (ghost aim line, cushion reflection with incoming and outgoing angles measured from the cushion's face and labelled equal, equal-mass elastic collisions that exchange the velocity components along the line of centres so momentum visibly hands over, speed arrows, pause/step, simple potting with stated simplifications), a ballistics launcher in the Angry Birds style on an honest scale (60 m range, real metres and seconds, g = 9.8, no air resistance — stated on the page; dotted trajectories kept for comparison, a crate target at 45 m, and a same-speed three-angles compare), a pendulum bench (period from string length only) and a seesaw bench (weight x distance), four kitchen-table experiment cards (balloon rocket, egg drop, paper airplane lab, pendulum painting), a verified links shelf (PhET Projectile Motion, PhET Collision Lab, The Physics Classroom, Khan Academy Physics) plus the 'Read deeper — Wikipedia' group Steven asked for on the Electronics pattern (Physics, Classical mechanics, Projectile motion, Momentum), a plain-language workshop on reflection/momentum/parabolas/the pendulum/torque, and a Help menu with full documentation. No upstream original exists; the collection copy is the maintained original.
